overview: Thomson Reuters is a content-driven technology company that powers business-critical professions -- legal, tax, audit, accounting, government and media -- with proprietary content, workflow software and increasingly agentic AI. Its flagship products include Westlaw and CoCounsel Legal for law firms, ONESOURCE and Checkpoint for tax/audit/accounting professionals, CLEAR for risk and investigations, and the Reuters News Agency. The company is headquartered in Toronto, files as a Canadian foreign private issuer (40-F/6-K, IFRS, USD reporting currency, December fiscal year-end), is dual-listed on the TSX and Nasdaq, and is majority-controlled (~70%) by The Woodbridge Company, the Thomson family holding vehicle.

business_model.summary: Thomson Reuters sells information, software and AI-enabled workflow solutions mostly on recurring multi-year subscription contracts (81% of 2025 revenue), supplemented by volume-based transactions revenue (12%, e.g., tax filings, SafeSend, SurePrep, Confirmation) and a structurally declining print business (Global Print, ~7%). Reported in five segments -- Legal Professionals, Corporates, Tax Audit & Accounting Professionals (together the 'Big 3', ~82% of revenue), Reuters, and Global Print -- the company monetizes a century of proprietary, expert-curated legal/tax content (1.9 billion documents, 1,500+ attorney editors, the West Key Number System) by embedding it, and now agentic AI built on it (CoCounsel), directly into customer workflows. Approximately 450,000 customers; largest single customer (the Reuters/LSEG news supply agreement) is ~5% of revenue. ~72% of 2025 revenue was U.S.-based.

revenue_streams.name: Legal Professionals (Westlaw, Practical Law, CoCounsel Legal)
Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals (Checkpoint, UltraTax, SafeSend, SurePrep)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2G -- law firms, corporate legal/tax/compliance departments, accounting and audit firms (including the seven largest global accounting firms), courts and government agencies, plus media organizations and consumers via Reuters News
business_model.geographic_mix: United States ~72% of 2025 revenue; remainder primarily U.K., Canada, Brazil, and other Europe/Asia-Pacific/Latin America markets

competitive_position.market_position: Leader in its 'Big 3' segments and in Reuters; operates in an estimated $31 billion addressable market for legal, tax and risk content/workflow software that management expects to grow 8-11% annually over the next five years. CoCounsel has the largest installed base of any legal AI tool (over 1 million professional users across 107 countries as of early 2026), ahead of LexisNexis Protege and well ahead of pure-play legal AI startups such as Harvey (~$11bn private valuation as of March 2026).

moat_factors.description: 1.9 billion documents, 1,500+ attorney editors and 2,500+ subject matter experts producing 1.6 million editorial enhancements per year; the West Key Number System (35 million legal classifications) and KeyCite (1.4 billion citation relationships) are decades-deep taxonomies competitors cannot easily replicate

Products (Westlaw, ONESOURCE, Checkpoint, CLEAR) are deeply integrated into daily professional workflows; 92% customer retention rate in 2025 and ~450,000 customers with no single customer over 5% of revenue

moat_factors.factor: Legal precedent protecting content from AI scraping
moat_factors.description: Third Circuit Court of Appeals upheld Thomson Reuters' copyright win against Ross Intelligence (Sept 2026), the first appellate ruling confirming AI competitors cannot train on Westlaw's proprietary headnotes/content without licensing -- reinforces the content moat against low-cost AI entrants

moat_factors.factor: Brand and trust in regulated, high-stakes workflows
moat_factors.description: Decades of accuracy/reliability in legal, tax and audit domains gives Thomson Reuters credibility for AI outputs in regulated environments where errors carry litigation/compliance risk, versus generalist LLMs
81% recurring revenue and multi-year contracts (1-5 years) support revenue stability, though renewal lag means revenue is also slower to re-accelerate in upturns
Largely fixed cost base (58% of expenses are staff costs) allows adjusted EBITDA margin to expand with revenue growth (39.2% in 2025, +100bp guided for 2026)

weaknesses: Reliance on legacy research/content subscription pricing that AI-native and consumption-based competitors could undercut
Global Print in structural decline (-6% in 2025) as a permanent revenue drag
Reuters segment margin under pressure (-320bp in 2025) from AI content licensing softness and higher investment
Woodbridge's ~70% controlling stake and the Founders Share limit M&A/takeover optionality and governance influence for minority shareholders
High U.S. revenue concentration (72%) creates sensitivity to U.S. legal/accounting/government spending cycles

growth_drivers: Broadening adoption of CoCounsel (Legal, Tax & Audit) -- 1 million+ professional users as of Feb 2026, next-generation agentic version built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK launched August 2026, with Deep Research grounded in Westlaw/Practical Law
'Big 3' segment organic growth acceleration -- 9% organic growth in FY2025, Big 3 guided to ~9.5-10.0% organic growth for FY2026 (raised from 7.5-8.0% after a strong Q2 2026)

Secular tailwinds: rising regulatory/compliance complexity (global minimum tax, e-invoicing mandates, cross-border tax/trade rules) and talent shortages in tax/audit/accounting professions driving automation demand

Tuck-in M&A to add AI-native capabilities: SafeSend and Additive (tax automation), TimeBase (Australian legal content), Noetica (deal intelligence, Feb 2026) -- continuing a steady cadence of $0.8-1.0bn/year in acquisitions
International expansion of legal/tax content and AI workflows into Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East
Operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base driving adjusted EBITDA margin expansion (+100bp guided for 2026) as organic revenue growth outpaces expense growth

Capital return optionality: dividend raised 10% for the 33rd consecutive year, ongoing $600m buyback program, and a $605m return-of-capital/share-consolidation transaction (court- and shareholder-approved April 2026)

business.description: Well-funded, narrowly focused AI entrants (e.g., Harvey) and foundation-model vendors could erode Thomson Reuters' pricing power or disintermediate parts of its workflow stack; customers may also build internal AI tools, reducing dependence on third-party research platforms

business.risk: Commoditization of free/low-cost AI-generated legal and tax content
business.description: Public AI tools trained on freely available information could diminish the perceived premium of packaged proprietary content for some use cases, even though the Ross Intelligence ruling helps protect Thomson Reuters' own corpus
Revenue has declined mid-single digits annually for years as customers migrate online; a permanent, modest drag on consolidated growth

business.risk: Customer concentration in professional end-markets under cost pressure
business.description: Law firms, corporate legal/tax departments and accounting firms are increasingly cost-conscious and vendor-consolidating, which could pressure renewal pricing even with high retention

financial.description: ~19% of 2025 revenue and ~39% of operating expenses were non-USD (GBP, CAD, EUR, BRL, INR); FX swings affect reported growth and margins even though 2025 had no net impact

financial.risk: Rising net interest expense / lower cash balances
financial.description: Net interest expense increased 14% in 2025 as share buybacks and debt maturities reduced cash balances; 2026 guidance embeds a further step-up to $150-160 million
Material defined benefit plans were 94% funded as of Dec 2025; future contributions depend on market performance and are not fully predictable

regulatory.description: Enacted and potential future AI legislation (globally) could restrict how Thomson Reuters trains and deploys AI, require product/business-practice changes, or create compliance costs and liability exposure
Increasing regulatory scrutiny of consolidation in legal/tax/compliance software could constrain future tuck-in M&A
~$430 million paid under HMRC DPT assessments for 2015-2018 tax years related to since-divested UK affiliates; company is contesting and expects substantial refund, recorded as a receivable

macro.description: 72% of 2025 revenue is U.S.-based; government contracts are typically cancellable at will and subject to policy/budget changes; a U.S. slowdown or legal/accounting sector pullback would directly hit demand

Company cites an uncertain macro/geopolitical backdrop (tariffs, inflation, rates) as a risk to its 2026 outlook, though subscription revenue has historically proven resilient and slow to decline in downturns

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management sizes the 'Big 3' addressable market at ~$31 billion, growing 8-11% annually over the next five years, driven by regulatory/compliance complexity, AI adoption in professional services, and talent shortages pushing automation
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate -- 81% recurring subscription revenue with multi-year contracts makes the business resilient through downturns, though there is a lag effect (slower to decline, also slower to re-accelerate); transactions revenue (12%) and Reuters advertising/sponsorship are more cyclically exposed; Global Print is in secular, not cyclical, decline
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct exposure given modest net debt (0.6x net debt/adjusted EBITDA at YE2025, well below the 2.5x target ceiling) and investment-grade credit profile; indirect sensitivity via net interest expense on ~$2.2bn total debt and via customer spending on discretionary professional services
key_input_costs: Compensation/staff costs (58% of total expenses -- salaries, bonuses, SBC)
Technology/cloud infrastructure and AI compute costs

recent_developments.event: Third Circuit Court of Appeals upheld Thomson Reuters' 2025 copyright win against Ross Intelligence, confirming Ross unlawfully used Westlaw headnotes to train a competing AI legal search engine -- the first appellate ruling on AI-training copyright, reinforcing Thomson Reuters' content moat; stock rallied on the news
Launched the next-generation CoCounsel Legal AI ecosystem, rebuilt on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, offering fully agentic, end-to-end legal research-to-citable-work-product workflows

Reported Q2 2026 total revenue growth of 9% (organic 8%), with 'Big 3' organic growth accelerating to 10%; adjusted EBITDA up 10% to $745 million (38.1% margin); free cash flow up 29% to $727 million; raised full-year 2026 outlook to ~8.0% total/organic revenue growth (from 7.5-8.0%) and 'Big 3' organic growth to 9.5-10.0% (from ~9.5%)

Ontario Superior Court of Justice granted final approval for the $605 million return-of-capital and share-consolidation ('reverse stock split') transaction; shareholders had approved it April 28, 2026

Announced 2026 outlook alongside a 10% dividend increase (to $2.62/share annualized, 33rd consecutive annual increase, fifth consecutive 10% raise), a new $600 million share buyback program, the $605 million return of capital/share consolidation, and the acquisition of Noetica (deal intelligence AI)
Announced CoCounsel had reached 1 million professional users across 107 countries, and the rollout of agentic AI access to 120,000+ law students across 200+ law schools
Acquired Additive AI, a San Francisco-based startup automating U.S. federal tax document processing (K-1 forms), for the Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals segment

FY2025 results: revenue $7,476 million (+3% total/constant currency, +7% organic); 'Big 3' organic growth 9%; adjusted EBITDA margin 39.2% (+100bp); free cash flow $1.95 billion; diluted EPS fell 32% to $3.33 due to a non-recurring $468 million tax benefit in the 2024 comparative period, while adjusted EPS rose 4% to $3.92

guidance.management_commentary: Management reaffirmed confidence in the 'Big 3' segments' acceleration, crediting broadening CoCounsel adoption (1 million+ users), strong Legal Professionals and Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals organic growth, and continued operating leverage from a largely fixed cost base. The 2026 outlook assumes constant currency versus 2025 and excludes the impact of any future acquisitions or dispositions; management flagged ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, and evolving AI regulation, as the primary risks to achieving the outlook.

bull_case: CoCounsel has decisively won the early legal-AI adoption race (1 million+ users, largest installed base of any legal AI tool) by embedding agentic AI into an existing trusted workflow (Westlaw/Practical Law) rather than requiring customers to adopt a new platform

The Third Circuit's September 2026 appellate ruling against Ross Intelligence is a landmark legal precedent protecting Thomson Reuters' proprietary content from being used to train rival AI models without licensing -- strengthening, not weakening, the company's moat in the AI era

'Big 3' organic growth has accelerated through 2026 (10% in Q2) and guidance has been raised twice, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding on a largely fixed cost base -- a rare combination of accelerating growth and margin expansion at a mature, 80%+ recurring-revenue incumbent

Disciplined capital allocation: investment-grade balance sheet (0.6x net debt/EBITDA, well under the 2.5x target), 33 consecutive years of dividend growth, active buybacks, and a $605 million return-of-capital/share-consolidation transaction demonstrate shareholder-friendly capital deployment alongside continued AI investment

Clean corporate structure post-LSEG: Thomson Reuters fully exited its LSEG stake in 2024, removing complexity and volatility from an equity-method investment and freeing capital for core-business reinvestment and shareholder returns
bear_case: AI could still structurally compress the value of Thomson Reuters' core research/content subscriptions over time if agentic tools (from Thomson Reuters itself or rivals) make legal/tax research dramatically faster, reducing billable research hours and the pricing power of per-seat subscription models

Intensifying competition from both incumbents (RELX/LexisNexis Protege, Wolters Kluwer) and well-capitalized AI-native entrants (Harvey, at an ~$11 billion private valuation) could pressure CoCounsel's pricing or growth even with its current lead

Woodbridge's ~70% controlling stake and the Thomson Reuters Founders Share structurally limit takeover premiums, M&A optionality, and minority shareholder influence over governance and capital allocation decisions

High U.S. revenue concentration (72%) and reliance on law firm, corporate and government spending leave the business exposed to a U.S. legal/accounting sector slowdown, government budget cuts, or a broader macro downturn, despite subscription revenue stickiness

Valuation already reflects much of the AI optimism (forward P/E near 20x, consensus price targets implying only modest further upside from current levels), raising the bar for continued multiple expansion absent sustained outperformance versus raised guidance
